input_checks.detail: AI-BOM acquired. One Cisco AI BOM 1.10.0 scan (OpenAI gpt-6-luna over Chat Completions, reasoning_effort none, bounded settings) ran on the 153-file public source copy (revision cfa08c56..., frigate/detectors, frigate/config, docker/main). The scan completed and the output validates as CycloneDX 1.6. It reports exactly one machine-learning-model: yolov6n.hef (frigate/detectors/plugins/hailo8l.py:50), with no hash, purl, version or external reference. The agent removed the other two candidates (the Dockerfile COPY step and a file-extension check). The CPU model Frigate downloads (cpu_model.tflite, Dockerfile:138) is not reported. A registry lookup for yolov6n.hef failed and the tool logged a 'degraded' warning although the result status is success. The CLI exited 1 at --validate (jsonschema missing) before writing the file; the file was produced from the tool's scan cache with the network denied. The tool reported no token usage or cost. See docs/AIBOM_ACQUISITION.md.
input_checks.next_action: none for this scan; do not rerun without a new approval

notice: REAL PILOT, PARTIAL. Frigate v0.18.2 inspected from a source checkout; nothing was built or run. Declarations are curated source-readings by the researcher, not BOM contents. Evidence is captured verbatim from the pinned tree. Three real inventories are loaded, each from one named producer and bound to its own scan scope within the pinned revision: SBOM from Syft 1.51.1 (whole source directory), CBOM from cdxgen 12.9.0 (frigate/ package, source-only; it reported zero cryptographic assets), AI-BOM from Cisco AI BOM 1.10.0 (153 files; one model, yolov6n.hef). Loading three inventories is not a three-BOM verification. Increment 3 adds one bounded check on the Syft inventory (tflite_runtime). An earlier BOMBridge-generated hashlib inventory is kept only as historical research data and is not part of this graph.
